subject: Dedicated commit: throughput verification, latency targets, and fallback matrix
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@orchard.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: procure@orchard.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated commit — throughput & latency requirements (Orchard)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo. We're evaluating a Dedicated GPU pool to serve our realtime summarization and chat endpoints. A few concrete asks from my engineering and procurement teams so we can move toward an SOW:

- Target sustained throughput: 1.2M tokens/minute (approx 20k tokens/sec) across a 3-region footprint; peak bursts up to 40k tokens/sec for 60s windows.
- Latency targets: p50 < 90ms, p95 < 250ms for single-turn generation at typical 256-token contexts.
- Measurement method: we need a clear verification plan (scripts, steady-state definition, warmup, KV/cache behavior).
- Commitment: we plan to commit to a 12-month reserved spend if you can provide a discount ladder tied to guaranteed tokens/sec bands and credits for missed targets.

I've attached our latest requirements doc (orchard_requirements_v3.pdf). Please advise next steps and what evidence you need from us.

Best,
Alicia
VP Product, Orchard AI

[Attachment: orchard_requirements_v3.pdf]

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@orchard.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — throughput & latency requirements (Orchard)

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear asks and the doc. High level: we can structure a 12‑month reserved commit with three throughput bands (bronze/silver/gold) and a measurement-based SLA that triggers credits if we miss the guaranteed sustainable TPS.

Quick clarifications we need before drafting the SOW:
1) Are your 20k TPS and 40k burst numbers measured as "token-generation/sec" aggregate across all workers, or do you expect per-region guarantees?
2) Typical request size (avg tokens in + tokens out) and concurrency distribution (many small requests vs few large streams).

I'll loop in Laura (pricing) and Ben (commercial). Can we do a short call tomorrow to align on the verification plan?

—Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Orchard throughput request — draft pricing & verification thoughts

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Alicia's asks. My initial take (pricing + test plan) below.

Pricing/discount framing:
- Base commit band 0-10k TPS: list price.
- Commit band 10-25k TPS: 15% discount off list.
- Commit band 25-50k TPS: 25% discount off list (requires 12-month commit + 95% prepayment option or 18-month with monthly).
- Burst buffer: optional 10% burst capacity (billed at on-demand rates) included in Gold band.
- SLA credits: 5% of monthly invoice per missed SLO window (capped at 25% / month).

Verification methodology (high-level):
- Acceptance window: 72 hours of steady-state testing per region. Define steady-state as >10 minutes continuous execution with Cv < 8% for measured TPS.
- Warmup: 30 minute warmup before measurement to populate KV cache and model CUDA kernels.
- Test harness: we deliver a reproducible runner (redwood_throughput_test_plan.md + kvcache-warmup-script.sh) that uses the customer's request distribution (they must provide 1 hour of production traces or a synthetic distribution).
- Metrics: report tokens/sec (aggregate), requests/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency for generation, GPU utilization, cache hit-rate.
- Measurement rules: sustained TPS measured as median of rolling 5‑minute windows across the 72hr window; burst acknowledgment requires separate short-window tests (60s/300s).

Operational fallback matrix (if capacity constraints observed during ramp):
- Auto-route to compatible lower-cost model variant with identical API semantics (no schema changes).
- Throttle policy with graceful 429 + Retry-After headers and prioritized traffic lanes.

Attachments: draft test plan and warmup script included. Please review and I'll convert to SOW language once we confirm bands.

-Laura
Director, Pricing & Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
[Attachments: redwood_throughput_test_plan.md, kvcache-warmup-script.sh]

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@orchard.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Procurement Ops <procure@orchard.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — throughput verification, latency targets, and fallback matrix

Thanks Laura — that structure is clear and close to what procurement wants. Couple of follow-ups from engineering and procurement:

- Measurement windows: can we agree that the sustained TPS guarantee is the lower bound across the 3 regions (i.e., each region must meet its committed share)? We want per-region SLAs.
- For warmup: our production traces include long-tail dialogs (up to 1024 tokens). Will that require separate acceptance bands?
- For discounts: procurement requests the 25% band at 10% higher commit (i.e., they can guarantee 12 months at 28% higher committed spend) in exchange for earlier payment terms. Is Redwood open to negotiating this custom band?

If you can send a redline SOW with per-region throughput bands and the exact acceptance script, procurement will take the draft to finance.

Best,
Alicia

From: ben.carter@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 15:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — throughput verification, latency targets, and fallback matrix

Alicia — quick note from commercial: we're open to a custom band to accommodate your finance ask. Proposed commercial adjustments: 

- Custom Gold-Plus band: 28% higher committed spend than Gold band => 30% discount. Requires 12-month prepay or 18-month with 50% upfront.
- Per-region guarantees: we can do per-region committed TPS bands but need to define failover rules (if one region suffers outage we will auto-shift traffic; credit only if global and per-region tests both fail).

Next steps:
1) Marissa / Laura to produce a redline SOW with the revised bands and the per-region acceptance script embedded.
2) Alicia to provide a 1-hour sample of production traces (anonymized) and preferred test window.

If we get those today, I'll escalate pricing approval and aim to have a draft SOW by EOD Thursday.

—Ben
